--- order: 1 unit: layers node: [AC9TDI10K02 n1, AC9TDI10K02 n2] introduces: [web-layers] title: Three layers summary: "A web page is content (the words and pictures), structure (HTML tags saying what each part is) and presentation (CSS saying how it looks). Swap the style sheet and only the look changes; show the structure and see the tags underneath." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "One page, three completely different looks, and not a single word changed. What did change?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8486 url: http://127.0.0.1:8486/index.html readySelector: ".wdview" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: web.yml#explain-pic, caption: "The club page: its content (the words), its structure (header, headings, a list) and its presentation (the Ocean style sheet)." } explainClip: query: { code: "@web.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Content, structure, presentation" say: "The same page, three style sheets." clip: - click: Ocean - wait: 800 - click: Poster - caption: { text: "Each style sheet changes only the look: the presentation.", say: "A new style sheet changes only the look." } - wait: 1200 - click: "Show structure, off" - caption: { text: "Underneath, the structure stays the same: header, h1, nav, h2, a list.", say: "The structure underneath never changed." } - wait: 1400 - click: "Style sheet, on" - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "Style sheet off" } - caption: { text: "Style sheet off: the content and structure are all still there, in the browser's plain look.", say: "Switch the style off, and the words and structure are still there." } - wait: 1500 --- Every web page you read is built in three layers: **content** (what it says), **structure** (what each part is) and **presentation** (how it looks). You don't need to write code to see them: this board takes one page apart. ## Predict: style sheet off ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to what is left without the style sheet tests the new move: presentation is a separate layer from the content and structure." check: type: predict q: "You switch off a web page's style sheet (its CSS). What is left?" options: ["All the words, headings and lists, in a plain look", "A blank page", "The colours, but no words", "Nothing changes at all"] actual: "Everything except the look: the words (content) and the headings, list and menu (structure) are all still there, in the browser's plain default style." ``` ## Try: swap the look ```step stage: run insight: "Swapping style sheets and switching the style off settles the prediction: only the presentation changes." try: { playground: board, starter: "web.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Try at least two style sheets and show the structure. Then switch the style sheet off. What is left?", when: "n >= 2 and e = 1 and p = 0", explain: "The words and the structure (header, headings, list) are all still there. The style sheet only ever held the look." } ``` Was your prediction right? ## Worked example: one part, three layers ```step stage: investigate insight: "Splitting one heading into its three layers models the new move. Sam thinks a style sheet changes what a part is, the misconception planted after the method." tasks: - check: type: sort q: "Which layer is each one?" options: ["Content", "Structure", "Presentation"] items: - ["The words \"Bring a friend!\"", "Content"] - ["A photo of the robot", "Content"] - ["

marking \"This week\" as a heading", "Structure"] - ["
    and
  • marking the list", "Structure"] - ["
    marking the menu", "Structure"] - ["color: teal", "Presentation"] - ["font-size: 30px", "Presentation"] - ["The page's background colour", "Presentation"] explain: "Content is what it says; structure is what each part is (HTML tags); presentation is how it looks (CSS rules)." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#sam" text: "Sam compares the Plain and Poster styles. Click the line where it first goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: looks-is-structure explain: "Line 3: the style sheet changes how \"This week\" looks, never what it is. It is an h2 heading in every style. To make it a list item you change the HTML (structure)." - check: type: question q: "You want every heading on the page to be purple. Which layer do you change?" options: ["Presentation: one CSS rule", "Structure: change every heading tag", "Content: retype the headings", "All three"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The tags say what the parts are; colour is the look.", "The words stay the same.", "Only the look changes."] explain: "h2 { color: purple; } in the style sheet: one rule, and the HTML is untouched." ``` ### "This week", layer by layer ```worked \text{content: } \textit{This week} :: The words on the page. \text{structure: } \texttt{

    This week

    } :: The HTML tag says it is a level-2 heading. \text{presentation: } \texttt{h2 \{ color: teal; font-size: 20px; \}} :: The CSS rule says how every h2 looks. \text{change the style sheet} \Rightarrow \text{only presentation changes} :: Same words, same tag, a new look. ``` Now sort the parts of the page. ### Find the mistake ### Which layer? ## Vary: change one layer ```step stage: modify insight: "Each task changes one layer and checks the others stay put: a colour, a size, then the content itself (in the HTML), not the look." try: { playground: board, starter: "web.yml#css", height: 640 } tasks: - starter: "web.yml#css" check: { type: board, text: "In the style sheet, make the main heading (h1) a different colour. Did the structure or the words change?", when: "a = 1 and u = 1 and d = 1", explain: "Add or change a rule such as h1 { color: crimson; }. The look changed; the structure and the words didn't." } - starter: "web.yml#css" check: { type: board, text: "Now make every h2 heading at least 28 pixels tall, with one rule.", when: "f >= 28 and u = 1", explain: "h2 { font-size: 30px; } changes both h2 headings at once, because the rule applies to every h2." } - starter: "web.yml#html" check: { type: board, text: "This time edit the HTML: change the words \"This week\" to \"Today\". Which layer changed?", when: "d = 0 and u = 1 and t >= 1", explain: "The content changed; the structure (still an h2) and the look didn't." } ``` ### Colour ### Size ### Content ## Practise: which layer? ```step stage: practise insight: "Naming the layer for everyday changes is the same move in mixed forms, plus a review of how text is stored." tasks: - check: type: question q: "The school site gets a dark mode. Which layer changes?" options: ["Presentation", "Content", "Structure"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The words stay the same.", "The headings stay headings."] explain: "Dark mode is a different style sheet: only the look." - check: type: question q: "The page is translated into French. Which layer changes?" options: ["Content", "Presentation", "Structure"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The look can stay the same.", "Headings stay headings in French too."] explain: "The words change; the structure and look can stay." - check: type: question q: "Three lines of text become a bulleted list. Which layer changes?" options: ["Structure", "Content", "Presentation"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The words are the same.", "The bullets come from the list structure, not a style."] explain: "Wrapping them in
      and
    • tags changes what they are: a list." - check: type: question q: "Review: how does the computer store the word \"Hi\" in the page?" options: ["As numbers: one character code for each letter", "As a picture of the letters", "As the CSS rules", "It isn't stored"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Text is stored as codes; the look comes later.", "CSS is how it looks, not what it says.", "Everything on a computer is stored."] explain: "H is 72 and i is 105: content is numbers too." ``` ### Dark mode ### French ### A list ### Review: text ## Make: a new look ```step stage: make insight: "Restyling the whole page without touching the HTML reverses the process: from a look you want to the presentation rules that make it." try: { playground: board, starter: "web.yml#make", height: 640 } hint: ["Only the style sheet box is yours to change.", "Try body { background: …; } and h1 { color: …; }.", "For example body { background: black; color: white; } and h1 { color: gold; }."] check: { type: board, text: "Give the page a completely new look: a new background and a new heading colour, without changing the HTML.", when: "g = 1 and a = 1 and u = 1 and d = 1", explain: "New presentation, same content and structure. That separation is what lets one site have many looks." } ``` Then: open any website and imagine its style sheet switched off. What would its structure be? ```teacher summary: Students swap style sheets, show a page's structure and switch the style off to separate content, structure and presentation, then change one layer at a time (AC9TDI10K02 nodes 1 and 2), with no coding needed. time: 40 timing: Predict and Try 6 min · Worked example 10 min · Vary 12 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can name the three layers of a web page. - I can say which layer a part or a change belongs to. - I can change the look of a page without changing its structure or words. struggle: Students judge parts by how they look. Keep asking "what is it?" before "how does it look?", and use the Structure button to check. before: > Try the boards yourself. The one idea: content, structure and presentation are separate layers. This is a Knowledge and understanding lesson: students read and tweak a style sheet but never have to write a page. The Code pathway's HTML & CSS course is where they build pages (its Rules and selectors lesson links back here). Node 2's minimum width asks students to write a small page; here they edit an existing one, which covers the explanation part. Students who want to write their own can open the HTML & CSS course's first lesson. Hands-on: in a browser, many sites can be seen without their style sheet (Firefox: View › Page Style › No Style; Safari's Reader view is similar). running: - "Predict: students who said a blank page think the style sheet holds the words." - "Try: ask what stayed the same across all three looks." - 'Worked example: for each sorted item, ask "what it says, what it is, or how it looks?"' - "Vary: after the content change, ask which layer a translator would change." - "Make: compare looks; ask whether anyone needed to touch the HTML." stuck: - see: A student says the Poster style made new headings (Sam's mistake). ask: Turn on Structure. Are the tags the same in every style? fix: "Yes: the style sheet changes looks only." - see: A student's CSS does nothing. ask: Is the rule's selector a tag on the page (h1, h2, p, li)? Is there a semicolon and a closing brace? fix: Fix the selector or the punctuation. stretch: Find a website with a dark mode switch. Which layer does the switch change, and how could you tell? support: "A three-column card: Content (what it says), Structure (what it is), Presentation (how it looks), with an example of each." leads: | Next: Why keep them apart (sites, phones, screen readers). Put to work in: Code › HTML & CSS (writing pages and style sheets). exit: q: Give one example of each layer from a web page you use, and say which layer a dark mode changes. a: "For example: the article text (content), its headings and lists (structure), its colours and fonts (presentation). Dark mode changes presentation." explain: > A web page is three layers: - **Content**: what it says (the words, pictures and links). - **Structure**: what each part is, marked with HTML tags (heading, paragraph, list, menu). - **Presentation**: how it looks, set by CSS rules in a style sheet (colours, fonts, sizes, layout). Change the style sheet and only the look changes: the words and the structure stay the same. class: inquiry: q: Take the style off a web page. What is left? prompts: - What is the page made of? - Which parts did the style change? notes: Content, structure, style. Let students predict before the board. activities: - at: predict kind: activity title: Strip it back minutes: 5 do: > Show a page, then its plain version with no style. Students name what disappeared and what stayed. notes: The look goes; words and structure stay. - at: modify kind: discussion title: Which layer? minutes: 3 do: > Sort: a heading, a colour, the words, a list, a font. Which layer is each? notes: Structure, style, content, structure, style. questions: - at: investigate title: Which layer? type: question q: A page's headings and lists belong to which layer? options: - Structure - Style - Content only - None of them answer: 0 explain: Structure says what each part is; style says how it looks. ```

# Sam's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: sam
In the Plain style, "This week" is a heading.
In the Poster style, "This week" is pink and huge.
So the Poster style changed "This week" into a different kind of part.
To make it a list item, Sam should change the style sheet.
# endregion
